news.title: All Whites captain coy on Fifa World Cup verdict, ahead of NZ football review
news.lede: Three months on from the All Whites’ Fifa World Cup exit, captain Chris Wood is still yet to fully get over the pain. That was the obvious conclusion from his interview with New Zealand media on Wednesday night, soon after he joined the team in Japan for the Kirin Cup, especially with a succinct eight-word summary. “We know we left a lot out there,” Wood said when asked for his initial reflection on the tournament. The last time we had seen Wood was in the depths of BC Place Stadium in Vancouver, after the All Whites’ 5-1 defeat to Belgium on June 27.

news.title: 2027 AFCON (Q): Gyan’s 2010 World Cup miss sparked my love for African football – McKinstry
news.lede: The Gambia head coach Jonathan McKinstry has revealed that his connection with African football dates back to Ghana’s memorable run at the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa. McKinstry made the revelation after guiding The Gambia to a 4-2 victory over the Black Stars at the Accra Sports Stadium in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. Reflecting on his long-standing connection with the continent, the Northern Irish coach recalled watching Ghana striker Asamoah Gyan miss a crucial penalty against Uruguay in the 2010 World Cup quarter-final. “I watched Asamoah Gyan miss the penalty at the 2010 World Cup.

news.title: Dropping Kelly and Toone could prove a World Cup masterstroke by Wiegman | Tom Garry
news.lede: England’s coach has given a wake-up call to her whole squad by leaving out two heroes of 2022 and 2025. Sarina Wiegman sent a clear message to two of England’s biggest names on Tuesday and – in doing so, irrespective of reputations – fired the same warning to every player: perform for your club or you will not go to the World Cup. Wiegman was unequivocal with her reasoning for leaving Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly out of her squad for October’s playoff against Greece. Her straight-to-the-point and typically honest style made it inescapably clear, when she said: “The main reason is that I think the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”

PTI Photo by Manvender Vashist *** Local Caption *** Vikash Dhorasoo advocates Indian football growth, dual citizenship for athletes, and mentoring India’s talent to reach global stages. CHENNAI When Vikash Dhorasoo played for the French national team at the 2006 FIFA World Cup, there were very few people who believed that an Indian could excel on football’s world stage. Ever since Dhorasoo made his debut for Les Bleus, the belief has grown that Indian footballers can do well at the world level.

news.title: Football: Uruguay reach Kolkata, Brazil due on Thursday | Football News
news.lede: Fresh from their 4-1 win against South Korea, Uruguay arrived here on Monday evening for next week’s football friendly against India. A group of players also got a feel of the conditions at Salt Lake stadium where they will play India on October 6. With five-time world champions Brazil due to check in on Thursday, the city will, for the first time, host teams who have won the World Cup multiple times. Winners of the 1930 and 1950 World Cup, Uruguay are ranked 20th in the world.Coached by Diego Forlan, who replaced Marcelo Bielsa after a disappointing World Cup, Uruguay are here without skipper Federico Valverde.

news.title: Former France Star Vikash Dhorasoo Believes India Can Reach FIFA World Cup
news.lede: Vikash Dhorasoo, the first Indian-origin player in a FIFA World Cup, expresses strong belief in India's potential to reach football's biggest stage. Visiting India for a friendly match against Brazil, Dhorasoo highlights the importance of method, clear objectives, and leveraging players of Indian origin to elevate the national team's level. He also offers his coaching expertise to help develop young talent in India.
